questionsToConsider: What are the standards your reviewers check against? Replace the grid rows with your own checklist.
What counts as minor, major and critical for your work? Write the definitions into the options so reviewers agree.
Who gets told when a review fails, and how quickly?
Do you need evidence for every issue, or only for major and critical ones?
guide.howToUseResponses: Filter by result and severity each week so critical findings never sit unread. Look at the grid across many reviews to find the standard that fails most often, since that points at a process problem rather than one bad item. Track the fix owners and due dates to closure, and compare reviewers' results on similar items to check they are applying the standards the same way.
customizeSteps: Rewrite the grid rows and the item types to match what your team actually reviews.
Put your own definitions of minor, major and critical into the severity options.
Share the link with reviewers or bookmark it on the inspection device, and export the results to CSV for your monthly quality report.

faqs.q: What is a quality assurance survey?
faqs.a: It's a structured form a reviewer fills in to record what they checked, what they found and what needs fixing, so every review is logged the same way.

faqs.q: What should a QA checklist include?
faqs.a: The standards being checked, a clear result, a description of each issue with its severity, supporting evidence and who owns the fix by when.
Yes. The evidence question accepts images and PDFs, up to five files per review.

faqs.q: How do I keep reviewers consistent?
faqs.a: Define each severity level in plain words, use the same checklist every time, and now and then have two reviewers check the same item and compare.
